$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.34,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.34/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and f2a09d17c9938eb500e061e999d882f97d35edd0e9678c31b15ae83e6aad309f and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.34/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
f2a09d17c9938eb500e061e999d882f97d35edd0e9678c31b15ae83e6aad309f is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
